question.problem: Let $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where ${b}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=2{c}_{1}?$

current_example.problem: Let $\mathcal{B}= \left\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \right\}$ be a basis of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274943/assets/7c185476a9b562ae6ea7e4300c251199236a79d9e214e3ac6b1e5a39d0c2201b.svg) What are the coordinates of $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}= \left\{ \mathbf{c}_1, \mathbf{c}_2 \right\},$ where $\mathbf{c}_1 = -\mathbf{b}_2$ and $\mathbf{c}_2 = -3\mathbf{b}_1?$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274943/assets/8f0f7042fb246b1d9b3a9238df249e42f7c6b69296b85d956621011099411447.svg) we can write $\mathbf{x}$ in terms of the vectors $\mathbf c_1$ and $\mathbf c_2,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2} \\  & =-2{b}_{2}+5{b}_{1} \\  & =2(-{b}_{2})-\frac{5}{3}(-3{b}_{1}) \\  & =2{c}_{1}-\frac{5}{3}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274943/assets/c36981f3b06429d3f7dba4db85c87720c0b99c519d783b7354224b915d33bbb5.svg)
